title: Machine for Updating a Configuration Record
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $Q,T$ be finite decidable types, let $M$ be a deterministic $k$-work-tape machine over the binary alphabet with state type $Q$, and let $u:T\to\operatorname{Option}(\{0,1\})\to T$ satisfy $u(\tau,\mathrm{blank})=\tau$ for every $\tau\in T$. There are a natural number $K$, a finite decidable state type $P$, a deterministic machine $R$ with $K+1$ work tapes over the record alphabet, entry and distinct yes/no states, and a constant $C$ such that the following holds. If a configuration $c$ has all work-tape heads and all nonblank cells within distance $s$ of the origin, and a configuration $d$ starts in the entry state with tape $0$ encoding the joined record of $c$ and tag $\tau$, while its other work tapes are blank, then $R$ reaches a configuration after at most $C(|\langle\operatorname{record}(c,\tau)\rangle|+|x|+1)$ steps without visiting either decision state earlier; through that time every work-tape head moves by at most $C(|\langle\operatorname{record}(c,\tau)\rangle|+1)$. If the one-step successor of $c$ remains within distance $s$ on all tapes, the final state is yes and tape $0$ contains its joined record, with tag updated by applying $u$ to $\tau$ and the output symbol emitted by $M$ (a blank output leaves the tag unchanged); otherwise the final configuration is the original one with state changed to no.
